name: 1. FC Köln

C.evidence: Averaged 49,918 (near-full RheinEnergieStadion, 50,000) in 2025-26; loud Südkurve with Wilde Horde ultras; crowds held up through repeated relegations and 2. Bundesliga seasons.

V.evidence: Member club (150,000+ members); regional sponsors (REWE front, DEVK sleeve), no betting or arms sponsors; women's team in Frauen-Bundesliga; strong academy. Very large DFB fines for fan pyrotechnics (EUR 924k in 2024-25; EUR 220k for 110 pyros v Bayern, Jan 2026).

H.evidence: Inaugural Bundesliga champion 1963-64, three league titles, 1978 double, four DFB-Pokals, 1986 UEFA Cup final.

O.evidence: Professional arm fully held by 1. FC Köln e.V. with no outside investor; members elect the board. Governance lapses (FIFA transfer ban 2023) and frequent coaching/board changes.

S.evidence: Promoted as 2. Bundesliga champion 2024-25, finished 14th in 2025-26; energetic, direct football under Kwasniok, now René Wagner. No lasting pressing identity.

flags: DFB named Köln the top-fined club for fan misconduct (mostly pyrotechnics). Decide if pyro-heavy fines should count as 'violence'; I did not apply an adjustment.

name: Bayer Leverkusen

C.evidence: BayArena (30,210) averaged 30,016 in 2025-26; first German fan scene to call itself Ultras, but atmosphere is modest by Bundesliga standards and travelling support is small.

V.evidence: Sponsors BarmeniaGothaer (front) and Niedax (sleeve), no betting/arms; funded women's team in Frauen-Bundesliga; decent academy. No notable positives beyond that.

H.evidence: UEFA Cup 1988, DFB-Pokal 1993, 2002 Champions League final; 2023-24 unbeaten Bundesliga and cup double with a record 51-match unbeaten run.

O.evidence: Wholly owned by Bayer AG under a 50+1 exemption as a works club; run competently and stably, but no member control.

S.evidence: Pressing, possession-heavy identity under Xabi Alonso (2022-25); since then Ten Hag, Hjulmand and Carles Martínez Novell; finished 6th in 2025-26.

flags: Company-club exemption from 50+1 is structural; no adjustment applied (not state, PE or multi-club). Decide if a structural penalty is wanted.

C.evidence: Averaged 51,100 at Borussia-Park (54,057) in 2025-26; big, loyal Nordkurve; stadium opened 2004 (not recent).

V.evidence: Member club (about 93,000 members); regional sponsors (Reuter Gruppe front, Sonepar sleeve), no betting/arms; established academy.

H.evidence: Five Bundesliga titles in the 1970s, two UEFA Cups (1975, 1979), 1977 European Cup final; the 'Fohlen' era is a landmark of German football.

O.evidence: Borussia VfL 1900 e.V. is member-run; no outside investor.

S.evidence: Finished 12th in 2025-26, poor start to 2026-27 (four straight losses); coaches Seoane, Polanski, now Blessin. No current pressing identity.

name: Eintracht Frankfurt

C.evidence: Averaged 59,071 at Deutsche Bank Park in 2025-26; one of Europe's biggest away followings (about 30,000 at Camp Nou, 2022); choreographies and a very loud Nordwestkurve.

V.evidence: Members' club with a public anti-racist stance (ex-president Peter Fischer's 2018 line against AfD members); sponsors Indeed (front) and Deutsche Vermögensberatung (sleeve), no betting/arms; women's team in Frauen-Bundesliga. Repeated fan disorder abroad lowers it slightly.

H.evidence: 1959 German champions, 1960 European Cup final (7-3 v Real Madrid), 1980 UEFA Cup, 2022 Europa League won unbeaten, five DFB-Pokals.

O.evidence: Eintracht Frankfurt Fußball AG is majority-held by the e.V. under 50+1, with minority holdings by friends/sponsor companies; stable and well run.

S.evidence: Riera (Jan-2026) then Adi Hütter; 8th in 2025-26. Transition-based football; intensity varies.

adjustments.evidence: Repeated UEFA sanctions for fan disorder: pyro and objects thrown at Camp Nou (2025-26 UCL, glass wall smashed) led to a two-match away-ticket ban while already on probation; earlier bans after Napoli 2023 and Marseille 2022 clashes.

flags: Violence -5 is my call from repeated UEFA sanctions; Kevin to confirm the scale.

name: FC Augsburg

C.evidence: WWK Arena (30,660, opened 2009) averaged 29,787 in 2025-26; steady crowds but little distinct atmosphere or away presence.

V.evidence: Local sponsors (WWK insurance front, Siegmund sleeve), no betting/arms. Nothing notable either way.

H.evidence: Top flight only since 2011; best finish 5th (2014-15) and one Europa League run (2015-16, out to Liverpool).

O.evidence: 50+1 applies, but the professional arm is investor-held via Hofmann Investoren GmbH: Bolt Football Holdings (David Blitzer) about 45%, Klaus Hofmann about 30%. Reports say Blitzer has explored selling.

S.evidence: 9th in 2025-26 under Wagner then Manuel Baum; pragmatic, no lasting pressing identity.

adjustments.evidence: David Blitzer's Global Football Holdings also invests in other clubs (e.g. Estoril Praia, Alcorcón, Beveren); Augsburg is not a feeder.

flags: Existing score had no multi-club adjustment; I added -4 for Blitzer's stake.

C.evidence: Averaged 56,947 at the Volksparkstadion (57,000) in 2025-26; crowds stayed near capacity through seven seasons in the 2. Bundesliga (2018-25); large, loud Nordtribüne.

V.evidence: HanseMerkur (front) and Plan International (charity, sleeve), no betting/arms; e.V. keeps control. Nothing strongly negative.

H.evidence: 1983 European Cup, 1977 Cup Winners' Cup, six German titles; the only club never relegated until 2018.

O.evidence: HSV e.V. holds about 75% of HSV Fußball AG; Kühne Holding cut its stake below 10% (Sparda-Bank 7.5%, Hanse & Raute 4.5%); club says no further major investors. Long history of boardroom instability.

S.evidence: Promoted 2025, 13th in 2025-26 under Merlin Polzin; active, front-foot football but not an elite press.

C.evidence: MEWA Arena (33,305) averaged 31,797 in 2025-26; Q-Block led by Ultraszene Mainz; compact and loud, carnival-club identity. A hooligan-leaning group (Schlechter Umgang) appeared in 2024.

V.evidence: Member club; Kömmerling (front) and iDM (sleeve), no betting/arms; known for climate-neutral and social commitments; fan project and academy pathway.

H.evidence: Top-flight since 2009 (and 2004-07); Klopp and Tuchel coaching roots; Conference League 2025-26 is their main European run.

O.evidence: 1. FSV Mainz 05 e.V., member-run, no outside investor.

S.evidence: High-intensity pressing lineage (Klopp, Tuchel, Svensson, Henriksen); Urs Fischer since Dec 2025 keeps an intense, compact style.

C.evidence: Europa-Park Stadion (34,700, opened 2021) averaged 34,118 in 2025-26; loyal and full, but atmosphere is good rather than intense. The new-stadium drop has lapsed (6th season).

V.evidence: Member club known for social/sustainability focus; strong academy pathway (Freiburger Fußballschule); women's team in Frauen-Bundesliga; Lexware and Edeka sponsors, no betting/arms.

H.evidence: No major trophies; long continuity (Streich era), 2022 DFB-Pokal final, 2025-26 Europa League run.

O.evidence: SC Freiburg e.V., member-owned and famously well run and stable.

S.evidence: 7th in 2025-26 under Julian Schuster; organised, hard-running team football.

name: SC Paderborn

C.evidence: Home Deluxe Arena (15,000) averaged 14,522 in 2025-26 in the 2. Bundesliga; small, fairly quiet support.

V.evidence: Local sponsors (C. Hedenkamp front, Mediacom sleeve), no betting/arms; nothing notable either way.

H.evidence: Third Bundesliga spell (2014-15, 2019-20, 2026-27); promoted via 2026 play-off win over Wolfsburg (2-1 aet).

O.evidence: SC Paderborn 07 e.V. under 50+1; past reliance on the late president Wilfried Finke; recent financial difficulties but stable now.

S.evidence: 'Brave football, young players' identity per coverage of the 2026 promotion; Ralf Kettemann coaches.

flags: Ownership detail (e.V. vs spun-off company, main backers) not fully verified.

name: SV Elversberg

C.evidence: Village club (Spiesen-Elversberg); stadium about 10,000; averaged 9,113 in 2025-26 in the 2. Bundesliga; lowest Bundesliga crowd so far in 2026-27 (9,307).

V.evidence: Main sponsor HYLO is the Holzer family's Ursapharm brand; no betting/arms; nothing notable either way.

H.evidence: First Bundesliga season (2026-27), first Saarland club in the top flight since 1993; rose from the Regionalliga in the 2020s.

O.evidence: Member club formally, but its rise is financed by the Holzer family and their company Ursapharm (Frank Holzer chairs the supervisory board; stadium and shirt carry Ursapharm brands).

S.evidence: Attacking, possession-and-pressing style under Horst Steffen carried into the promotion side; Vincent Wagner now coaches.

flags: Patron-funded rise (Ursapharm): decide if an overspend adjustment fits; I did not apply one.

C.evidence: Averaged 61,829 in the 2. Bundesliga in 2025-26, by far the league's highest; huge, loyal Nordkurve that held up through three second-tier seasons.

V.evidence: Member club; financing through a members' cooperative (Auf Schalke eG) instead of an outside investor; Beumer Group and Blåkläder sponsors, no betting/arms; strong community identity.

H.evidence: Seven German titles (pre-Bundesliga era), 1997 UEFA Cup, five DFB-Pokals; a symbol of Ruhr working-class football.

O.evidence: FC Gelsenkirchen-Schalke 04 e.V. is fully member-controlled; members oppose spinning off the pro side. Debt of about EUR 162m and negative equity of about EUR 97m after years of mismanagement.

S.evidence: Won the 2. Bundesliga in 2025-26 under Miron Muslić; no lasting intense style in recent years.

name: TSG Hoffenheim

C.evidence: PreZero Arena in Sinsheim (30,150) averaged 26,697 in 2025-26, below capacity; small fan scene and limited identity.

V.evidence: SAP (front) and ProMinent (sleeve), no betting/arms. 2025-26 fan protests against Hopp associate and agent Roger Wittmann; executives dismissed after distancing themselves from him.

H.evidence: Village club lifted from the fifth tier to the Bundesliga (2008) by Dietmar Hopp's funding; no major honours.

O.evidence: Returned formally to 50+1 in Nov 2024, but a 2025-26 power struggle (Hopp backing Wittmann) led to dismissals and labour-court cases; member control looks limited in practice.

S.evidence: 5th in 2025-26 under Christian Ilzer; high-energy pressing style.

flags: Hopp-funded rise is historical: decide if an overspend adjustment (-2) should apply.

C.evidence: Anchor. Stadion An der Alten Försterei (22,012) averaged 21,996, almost all standing; fans rebuilt the stadium themselves (2008). Expansion to 40,500 planned; temporary move to the Olympiastadion from Dec 2027.

V.evidence: Member club with deep fan involvement; invests in its women's team (Frauen-Bundesliga, shared training centre being built); Raisin Bank and Kermi sponsors. Dec 2024 lighter thrown at Bochum's goalkeeper led to a points loss.

H.evidence: East German cult club (1968 FDGB-Pokal), survival stories (fans' 'Bleed for Union' blood donation), rise to the Champions League in 2023.

O.evidence: Anchor. 1. FC Union Berlin e.V., member-owned; stadium company share scheme sold to fans.

S.evidence: 11th in 2025-26; physical, direct, hard-running style; Mauro Lustrinelli coaches.

C.evidence: Weserstadion (42,100) averaged 41,265 in 2025-26; loud Ostkurve with anti-racist ultra groups; strong loyalty after the 2021 relegation.

V.evidence: Members' club with a long anti-discrimination and CSR record ('Werder bewegt'); regional sponsors (Matthäi, Ammerländer), no betting/arms; women's team in Frauen-Bundesliga.

H.evidence: Four German titles, 1992 Cup Winners' Cup, 2004 double; one of the Bundesliga's most-played clubs.

O.evidence: e.V. holds the majority of the KGaA; a regional alliance of Bremen businesspeople holds 19.71% on no-dividend, long-hold terms (expanded Sept 2026).

S.evidence: 15th in 2025-26; Steffen then Daniel Thioune. Front-foot but inconsistent.

name: Angers

C.evidence: Stade Raymond-Kopa (19,350) averaged 12,484 in 2025-26, among Ligue 1's lowest; ordinary atmosphere.

V.evidence: Local sponsors (club school, Maison de l'Atoll), no betting/arms. Former owner-president Saïd Chabane resigned in 2023 and was convicted in 2024 of sexually assaulting six female employees of the club and his company; his son now runs the club.

H.evidence: Coupe de France finals 1957 and 2017; long spells between the top two tiers.

O.evidence: Owned by the Chabane family (son Romain Chabane president) after the father's conviction; sale attempts have failed; DNCG placed transfer and wage restrictions for 2025-26.

S.evidence: 13th in 2025-26; defensive, low-possession side; Stéphane Gilli coaches in 2026-27.

flags: Ownership remains in the family of an owner convicted of sexual assault on club staff; confirm Values/Ownership treatment.

C.evidence: Stade de l'Abbé-Deschamps (18,541) averaged 16,313 in 2025-26 in a town of about 35,000; loyal, fairly traditional crowd.

V.evidence: Historic youth academy (Cantona, Cissé, Boli, Mexès); local sponsors, Groupama sleeve, no betting/arms.

H.evidence: Guy Roux's 44-year reign took a small-town club to the 1996 double and four Coupe de France titles; a model of French provincial football.

O.evidence: Majority owned (about 60%) by Chinese businessman James Zhou (ORG Packaging) since 2016; stable, modest investment.

S.evidence: 15th in 2025-26; Will Still appointed June 2026 (energetic, pressing approach at Reims and Lens).

name: Brest

C.evidence: Stade Francis-Le Blé (15,220) averaged 14,362 in 2025-26; compact, loud old ground; supporters strongly attached to it. A new 15,000 stadium at Guipavas is planned.

V.evidence: Breton regional identity; local sponsors (Quéguiner, Breizh Cola, Leclerc), no betting/arms; family-run community club.

H.evidence: First European campaign in 2024-25 (Champions League league phase and knockout play-off); earlier top-flight spells, 1980s Ginola era.

O.evidence: Owned and run by the local Le Saint family (Denis and Gérard); prudent budget.

S.evidence: 12th in 2025-26; organised, hard-working team; Julien Lachuer coaches 2026-27.

flags: The new-stadium move (Guipavas) is still pending; apply the -1 new-stadium rule when it opens.

name: Le Havre

C.evidence: Stade Océane (25,178, opened 2012) averaged 19,253 in 2025-26; average atmosphere.

V.evidence: Zeturf (betting) on shorts; strong academy record (Pogba, Mahrez, Mandanda, Lass Diarra).

H.evidence: France's oldest club (founded 1872), 1959 Coupe de France; famous academy.

O.evidence: Vincent Volpe sold his 96.2% stake in mid-2025 to Blue Crow Sports Group (Jeff Luhnow, Houston); supporters voiced concern about the club's identity.

S.evidence: 14th in 2025-26 under Didier Digard; low-possession, defensive side.

adjustments.evidence: Blue Crow Sports Group also owns CD Leganés, Cancún FC and Elite Falcons (UAE) and has pursued Monza; stated goal is to 'optimise talent flows'.

flags: Wikipedia's 2026-27 table still lists Volpe as chairman; verify the BCSG sale has completed (reported as agreed June 2025).

H.evidence: Top-flight spells 2003-04 and 2005-10 (Drogba, Gervinho era); rebuilt after 2013 bankruptcy; first top-flight season in 16 years.

O.evidence: Owned by OutField Inc, a Brazilian investment firm, with celebrity co-owners (Djokovic, Massa, Magnussen, Courtois).

S.evidence: Back-to-back promotions (National 2025, Ligue 2 2026) under Patrick Videira; limited top-flight evidence.

adjustments.evidence: OutField runs a multi-club model with Coritiba (Brazil).

C.evidence: Stade du Moustoir (16,787) averaged 15,382 in 2025-26; Merlus Ultras 1995 lead the Kop Sud; small, lively town-centre ground.

V.evidence: Breton regional identity; local sponsors (Jean Floc'h, Breizh Cola), no betting/arms.

H.evidence: 2002 Coupe de France; 18 top-flight seasons.

O.evidence: Loïc Féry remains chairman; Bill Foley's Black Knight Football Club holds a large stake.

name: Lyon

C.evidence: Groupama Stadium (59,186, opened 2016) averaged 49,848 in 2025-26; Bad Gones lead a loud Virage Nord.

V.evidence: Emirates (UAE state airline) main sponsor and Winamax (betting) on the back lower it; major academy (Benzema, Lacazette, Cherki) and the women's game's most successful club raise it.
